rationale: Interpret receipt 3324fe87d6da49c6b53eab0e116823df, the clean-copy repeat of the corrected transfer experiment. It reproduces the pair that the account rests on: the voter control installs the named target with an error-free future and no leaderless samples, while the transfer to a member whose own configuration reports non-voter completes without error, installs nobody, and leaves six 10 ms samples without a leader. The account therefore states the corrected result as observed twice and updates the disruption figures and sampling notes to cover three trigger runs. Conclusion and defect claim are unchanged.

knowledge.statement: Automatic leadership transfer and explicit leadership transfer use different target checks: pickServer (used when no id is given) skips every server whose Suffrage is not Voter, while an explicit id is only looked up in leaderState.replState, which contains an entry for every configured server including non-voters, and a successful lookup proceeds to replicate and send TimeoutNow without consulting the target's suffrage.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state with a committed latest configuration containing a non-voter; explicit LeadershipTransferToServer(id) for that member.

knowledge.statement: A voter that receives a RequestVote from a candidate absent from its latest configuration rejects it before any term handling, but a candidate that is present yet not a voter is handled later: the voter first adopts a higher term and steps down to follower, and only then rejects the vote because hasVote is false. timeoutNow performs no term, leader or membership check and immediately marks the receiver as a leadership-transfer candidate.
knowledge.conditions: Voter with a known latest configuration; RequestVote with LeadershipTransfer=true from a configured non-voter at a higher term.

interpretations.rationale: Conclusion: violated, and the scoped defect is asserted. A leadership transfer that explicitly names a member the configuration marks as a non-voter is admitted, completes its future without error, and does not install that member as leader; the attempt instead forces an election round in which every member's term advances, leadership lands on a member the caller did not name, and leadership is absent for a measurable interval. Evidence, four receipts of the same experiment lineage. Parsed index 1 of receipt d436029b08c5425aa5aec577901cb8ba and of successor receipt 0726bba116ac415fa38b99b96a88290f, the control where the explicit target is an ordinary voter: target_ever_leader=true, final_leader_is_target=true, future_ok=true, target_term_after=3 with other_member_term_max_after=3, so the mechanism installs the named target with a single term advance. Parsed index 3 of both receipts, the trigger where one non-leader member was demoted with DemoteVoter before the transfer: future_ok=true with an empty future_error, target_ever_leader=false, final_leader_is_target=false, target_term_after=4 and other_member_term_max_after=4, while the case event (parsed index 2) records target_demoted=true and transfer_target_role=nonvoter. A successor run, receipt 4185f1615cf54e4fbd4801044480416d, corrects the earlier measurement: the target's own configuration is read after DemoteVoter returns and polled until it changes (demotion_converged=true, demotion_converge_ms=0), and at the moment the transfer is requested the target itself reports target_role_in_own_config=nonvoter, so the member's own view already showed it held no vote; it still campaigned (7 candidate samples, 7 leaderless samples, target_term_after=4, target_ever_leader=false, future_ok=true with an empty error) while the voter control at parsed index 1 installed the named target and produced 0 candidate and 0 leaderless samples. In receipt 0726bba116ac415fa38b99b96a88290f the trigger produced 8 candidate samples with 8 leaderless samples (about 80 ms with no member reporting Leader) out of 470 samples at roughly 10 ms spacing, against 0 candidate and 0 leaderless samples out of 471 in that run's control. The two cases differ only in the target's suffrage, so the outcome difference is attributable to eligibility, not to the transfer path, harness or transport timing. Mechanism from source: leaderLoop resolves an explicit id only through leaderState.replState (raft.go:687-742), which startStopReplication populates for every configured server including non-voters, whereas the automatic path's pickServer skips non-voters outright (raft.go:2186-2206); leadershipTransfer replicates the target and sends TimeoutNow (raft.go:991-1023), and timeoutNow (raft.go:2232-2237) marks the receiver as a leadership-transfer candidate with no suffrage, term, leader or membership check; electSelf raises the target's term and asks every voter, whose requestVote handler adopts the higher term and steps down before rejecting the non-voter (raft.go:1696-1707). The trigger's term pattern (target and all other members at 4, one step beyond the rejected round) and its leaderless interval match exactly that path, while the control's single-step advance to 3 matches a successful transfer. Clean-copy repeat, receipt 3324fe87d6da49c6b53eab0e116823df (completed, tests_passed, exit 0): re-executing the corrected experiment from its retained inputs reproduced the pair. Parsed index 0, the voter control: target_role_in_own_config=voter, future_ok=true in 2 ms, target_ever_leader=true, final_leader_is_target=true, and 0 candidate and 0 leaderless samples out of 471. Parsed index 2, the trigger case: target_demoted=true, demotion_converged=true at 0 ms and target_role_in_own_config=nonvoter; parsed index 3: future_ok=true with an empty error in 2 ms, target_ever_leader=false, final_leader_is_target=false, 6 candidate samples and 6 leaderless samples (about 60 ms) out of 470, target_term_after=4 and other_member_term_max_after=4. The corrected result is therefore observed twice with the target's own configuration confirming the non-voter role at request time. Consequence under the exercised conditions: a caller that names a serving but non-voting member receives a completed transfer with no error, no transfer of authority, an extra election round that raises every member's term, and a leaderless interval whose length follows the configured election timeout.

knowledge.assertion: An explicit transfer target is resolved only through leaderState.replState, which includes non-voters, while pickServer skips non-voters.
A voter adopts a higher term and steps down before rejecting a configured non-voter candidate, and timeoutNow forces candidacy without checking suffrage or term.

counterevidence: The documentation's promise is soft rather than a guarantee: it says it is 'very likely' the target wins and that a follower which cannot be promoted 'will fail gracefully' (api.go:1296-1330), and the leaderLoop code deliberately reports nil with the message 'lost leadership during transfer (expected)', which can be read as the future reporting only that leadership was relinquished. The claim therefore rests on the admission of an ineligible target and on the observed outcome, not on the future's wording alone.

The control case shows the same mechanism transfers leadership correctly to a voter, so the defect is specific to the eligibility of an explicitly named target, not to leadership transfer in general. The repeat reproduced that control as well, with the named voter installed and no leaderless samples.

The measured disruption is small in absolute terms because the cluster ran with inmemConfig timeouts (Heartbeat/Election/Lease 50 ms): the three trigger runs recorded 8, 7 and 6 leaderless samples (about 80, 70 and 60 ms) and one extra election round, against zero leaderless samples in the voter controls. The interval follows the configured election timeout, so a production configuration of about 1 s would scale it accordingly; these millisecond figures are not a bound for other settings.

No committed entry was lost, no vote was counted for an ineligible candidate, and no decision-safety property was contradicted in either case; what is contradicted is the completion signal and the authority outcome of the explicit transfer.

Both corrected runs show the target's own configuration had already converged to non-voter before the request, so the exercised case is a member that knew it could not win; a demoted member whose own view still lagged (a stale configuration) was not exercised, although the earliest runs exercised an unknown mix.
limitations: Every run exercised one cluster size (four members, three voters after the demotion) and one relationship: a leader transferring to a non-leader member. Transfer initiated while the leader later regains leadership, and clusters whose only non-voter is the sole reachable member, were not tested.

Leaderless counts are sampled every ~10 ms over roughly 4.7 s of the 5 s window (470 to 471 samples); a gap shorter than the sample spacing would be missed, so 60 to 80 ms is a lower bound for the trigger and the controls' zero does not prove uninterrupted leadership.

Only immediate convergence was observed: in both corrected runs the demoted member's own view reported the new role within the first poll (0 ms), so no case exercised a target whose configuration still showed it as a voter at request time.
That the voter members had committed the demotion before the transfer is inferred from their rejection and term adoption, not from reading each voter's configuration.

Out of scope: whether an unprivileged or misconfigured peer could send TimeoutNow directly, even though timeoutNow performs no term, leader or membership check (raft.go:2232-2237); that path was not exercised here.
interpretations.joint_history: All four receipts belong to this investigation and were produced by successive revisions of the same fixed experiment under the same snapshot. Receipt d436029b08c5425aa5aec577901cb8ba is the first run; 0726bba116ac415fa38b99b96a88290f adds per-member state sampling and a role field that, because of harness ordering, was read before the demotion; 4185f1615cf54e4fbd4801044480416d moves that read after DemoteVoter returns and polls it, which is the revision that establishes the target's own view at request time. Receipt 3324fe87d6da49c6b53eab0e116823df is a clean-copy repeat of that third revision executed from its retained fixed inputs, with the same case names, admissions and assertions, so its events are directly comparable and it adds reproducibility rather than a different basis.
